0xb7.evidence: Handler 0x80074400 writes -1 into word0 of 16-byte record idx of the zone table [0x8007F1C8]. Sys_80 (add hotspot rect, slots 40-79 / 80-127) and bc (slots 0-39) fill those records (callback script address, rect x0,y0,x1,y1, type) and return the slot idx in G0; scripts keep it ('push G0; pop G0x1ec') and later do 'push G0x1ec; b7' (61 uses, e.g. after 'You found Dragonbane.').

0xb8.name: sin_deg
0xb8.args: stack: 1 word (angle in degrees, 16-bit); result in G0 (fixed point, +-4096 = 1.0)
0xb8.evidence: Handler 0x80078DD8 converts the 16-bit angle to the 4096-per-turn unit (x*4096/360 via the 0xB60B60B7 reciprocal) and returns func_80079324(angle) in G0; func_80079324 is a quarter-wave table lookup (table at 0x80083588, 1024/2048/3072 quadrant logic) = sine. Scripts: 'push G0x1f0 (angle, wrapped at 0x168=360); b8; push G0; pop L4; mul L4,3' i.e. circular motion. Checked: scales the angle by ~4096/360 and calls the sine routine 0x80079324; result in the accumulator.

0xb9.name: cos_deg
0xb9.args: stack: 1 word (angle in degrees, 16-bit); result in G0 (fixed point, +-4096 = 1.0)
0xb9.evidence: Same as b8 but calls func_800793B8, the same table with a 1024 phase shift = cosine. 2 uses in scene 0x143a2b44 together with b8 (x = r*cos, y = r*sin).

0xba.name: bgm_set_track_levels_timed
0xba.args: inline 2 words (stack 4): operand low byte = channel, word0 byte0/byte1 = two level bytes (0x00,0x40 / 0x00,0x80 / 0x01,0x80 / 0x00,0xBE), word1 = frames; 110 uses
0xba.evidence: Handler calls 0x8005B314(chan, a, b, frames): 0x80013F2C(sound object [0x8007FD8C], chan, a, b) rewrites the per-part level bytes of that channel at 0x8002B6C4+chan*2+k for every part k flagged in the mask table 0x8002B6C0 (mode byte 1: 'a != 0' flag; mode byte 2: the value b / a), then creates/refreshes the task 0x8005B3B0, which after 'frames' ticks calls 0x80013F2C(.., chan, 0, 0) to restore. So it temporarily overrides two level bytes of one music part for N frames. Used 110x in cutscenes at fixed times ('ba 0x4000 0x120', 'ba 0 0 2' to clear). What the two bytes are (volume/pan/mute of layered tracks) is not established; the 'temporary override then restore' part is certain.

0xbb.name: play_bgm
0xbb.args: inline 1 extra word: operand low16 = track id (0x8aa..0x8f3), word0 = mode byte (0 or 1, mostly 1); stack form pops the same two
0xbb.evidence: Handler 0x800789C4: if the id differs from ctx+0x38C it finds (or allocates) the pool task of type 0x800597B0, sets state 0 (or 10 = restart if one exists), +44 = id, +64 = byte param. That task calls cd_set_play_location/cd_set_play_mode, open_resource_stream, is_sequence_playing, sequence_track_tick, sound_restore_voice_snapshot = loads and plays a music sequence from the CD. 479 uses, almost always at scene start ('bb 0x8bc 1'), followed by a9 polling in a few scenes.

0xbc.name: add_trigger_zone
0xbc.args: inline 3 words (stack 5): operand low16 = flags word (0x401 / 0x800), word0 = callback script address, word1 = x0 | y0<<16, word2 = x1 | y1<<16; returns slot idx in G0
0xbc.evidence: Handler 0x8007426C finds the first free (word0 == -1) 16-byte record among slots 0..39 of [0x8007F1C8] and fills it: word0 = script address, +4/+6/+8/+10 = rect, +12 = operand low16, +14 = 2; stores the slot index in G0. Sibling of sys_80 (same table, slots 40..79/80..127, type from the operand). Scripts store G0 ('push G0; pop G0x1ec') for a later b7 removal, and place it among sys_80 hotspot definitions in clickable scenes (57 uses).

0xbd.name: nop_discard_args
0xbd.args: stack: pops 2 words (inline: skips 1 word); no effect
0xbd.evidence: Handler 0x80079000 only advances the data-stack pointer by 8 (stack form) or the ip by 4 (inline) and returns. Used 13 times, e.g. 'push 0; af; push G0; bd' in actor AI frame functions (scene 0x183100dc) or 'push 0; push.b G0x9a; bd' (0x17629c00): a stripped-out call whose arguments are discarded.

0xbe.name: set_msgbox_option
0xbe.args: inline 0 extra words: operand byte0 = option (0..6), byte1 = value (0/1; option 3 takes a frame count)
0xbe.evidence: Handler 0x8006F4C4 switches on the option: 0 = [0x8007F25C] bit24, 1 = [0x8007F260] bit23, 2 = [0x8007F260] bit24, 3 = halfword [0x8007FD70] = value, 4 = [0x8007F260] bit25, 5 = [0x8007F25C] bit23, 6 = [0x8007F264] bit10. The message-box engine reads them: option 3 is the window fade in/out frame count (0x8004CF0C, alpha ramp (frame<<7)/value; scripts use 0x3c = 60 and 0x1e = 30), option 2 gates drawing of the window frame (0x8004E840), option 4 gates the page-advance sound (0x8004D120), option 1 is copied into the message-box flags (+0x338, bit 23) when 0x92 opens a box (0x80074F20), option 5 is tested at 0x80053318 and 0x800751BC (box flag setup), option 0 when a box is created (0x80053018), option 6 at 0x8004DC28. 595 uses: 'be 0x100' (option 0 on) 184x and 'be 0x0' 132x mostly at scene/cutscene init, 'be 0x3c03' 38x (option 3 = 60 frames), 'be 0x101' 106x. Message-box configuration, so it matters for the dialogue analysis.

0xbf.name: call_script_next_frame
0xbf.args: inline 1 word (stack 1): word0 = script function address (e.g. 0xbe9, 0xc19, 0xbf9, 0xc09, 0xa5a)
0xbf.evidence: Handler 0x8006F634 allocates a pool task (type 0x8006F6C8) with +8 = address. The task frees itself, calls func_80071c70 (vm_call: pushes ip, frame regs and ctx+0x20C on the call stack and sets ip = codebase + addr*4) and ORs 0x70800 into ctx+0x20C. So the main script thread calls that function the next time it runs; several bf in a row chain (the last queued runs first and returns into the previous). 1178 uses; the addresses 0xbe9, 0xbf9, 0xc09, 0xc19 each occur ~207 times (clearly a set used together in 200+ scenes), others like 0xa5a/0xb35/0xb60/0xb71 are scene-specific functions.

0xc0.name: actor_scale_to
0xc0.args: operand low16 = actor id (negative = current actor); 2 inline words (or 2 stack values): target value (16.16 fixed, 0x10000 = 1.0), duration in frames (0 = set immediately)
0xc0.evidence: Shared handler 0x80076964 does not act: it appends command type 13 to the actor's 16-slot command ring (type byte at actor+0x80+slot, 2 arg words at slot*8) and returns. The type-13 executor 0x8003B2EC either stores the value in actor+0xB8 or spawns a ramp task (0x8003A460) that steps actor+0xB8 linearly over N frames and sets flag 0x40000000 in actor+0xE4 while running. actor+0xB8 is initialised to 0x10000 at actor creation and the sprite renderer (0x80038930..) divides vertex offsets by it, so it is a scale/zoom factor (note: inverse, values below 0x10000 enlarge). Scripts use 0xB000-0x14800 over 90-180 frames, e.g. 'c0 actor 0x10000 0xb4; 8a move; 74; c1'.

0xc1.name: actor_wait_scale_done
0xc1.args: operand low16 = actor id; no arguments
0xc1.evidence: Shared handler 0x80076964 queues command type 14 on the actor. Its executor 0x8003B39C checks flag 0x40000000 in actor+0xE4 (set by the c0 ramp task, cleared when it finishes); while set it sets the actor wait counter (+0xB4 = 1) and does not advance the command queue. It is a barrier in the ACTOR's queue, not a script wait. Always follows c0 in scripts (c0 ...; 74; c1).

0xc2.name: map_anim_control
0xc2.args: operand low16 = animation id; 1 inline word = (mode << 24) | value, or 3 stack values (top = id, then mode, then value). Modes: 0 = loop flag (bit0), 1 = ping-pong flag (bit1), 2 = pause (bit2; value 1 pauses, 0 resumes), 3 = speed/duration scale (halfword, 0x100 = normal, larger = slower), 4 = rewind to frame 0
0xc2.evidence: Finds the 16-byte entry whose halfword id matches in the scene-header table at [0x8007F0FC] (count at halfword 0x8007FD4A) and edits its flag byte (+11), speed halfword (+14) or frame/timer bytes (+12,+13); jump table at 0x8007E08C. The per-frame consumer (0x8004B350..) steps the frame index, reloads the timer as frame_duration*speed>>8 and blits the frame via 0x80023FF0, honouring pause/loop/ping-pong bits. Scripts pause ids 4,5 at scene start (mode 2 value 1) and un-pause them later. Exact visual (map tile/sprite animation) not confirmed.

0xc3.name: clear_actor_override
0xc3.evidence: Handler clears bit 0x2000 of the global flag word at 0x8007F25C and nothing else. That bit is set by op 0x7F (which also stores an actor index in ctx+0x3C5); op 0x7F with argument 0xFFFE clears it in exactly the same way. The per-frame actor-update function 0x8003B814 skips the normal update of the actor ctx+0x3C5 while the bit is set. So c3 = release the script's hold on that actor (counterpart of 0x7F).

0xc4.name: movie_open
0xc4.args: operand low byte = number stored in task+58 (observed 10,15,25,30; most likely frames per second); 2 inline words: resource/package id (0xDB3-0xDFA, 0x1300-0x1302), size = width (low16) | height (high16) e.g. 0x00F00140 = 320x240; then the VM waits one frame
0xc4.evidence: Handler is NOT in the field-engine RAM images: it lives in a separately loaded module (scene package part type 22, 78,812 bytes of MIPS, present only in scenes that use these ops; base 0x800BEA00: the handler addresses line up with the blob's function starts at that base and 0x8006C1AC passes the same constant; I read the blob from VALKYRIE.BIN in the scene packages I checked that use these ops). Handler: allocates a task (0x8002FC18) with task function 0x800BF714 and stores width/height (+48,+50), resource id (+52) and the operand byte (+58). The task function waits for cd_is_active() == 0, streams the resource from CD (cd_get_track_sector_info/cd_set_play_*), allocates frame buffers (full-screen 320x224+ gets a special path), decodes frames and builds textured GPU primitives. Used in ending/cut-scene scenes with 320x240 clips and small map overlays.

0xc5.name: movie_play
0xc5.args: operand low byte = byte stored in task+56 (observed 0x3c,0x45,0x46, 0; used as a draw priority/depth value); 1 inline word = x (low16) | y (high16) position (map coordinates minus camera; 0,0 for full-screen); or 3 stack values
0xc5.evidence: Module handler 0x800BFEEC: finds the movie task by its function pointer (0x8002FD10(0x800BF714)); if the task's state byte (+57) is still 0 (not loaded) it rewinds ip by 4 and waits a frame (blocks until loaded); otherwise stores x,y in +44/+46, the byte in +56 and sets flag bit 1 (start playing), which the task function needs to advance from state 1 to 2. Always directly follows c4.

0xc6.name: movie_stop
0xc6.evidence: Module handler 0x800BFFE0: if the movie task exists, sets its flag bit 2 (close request) and rewinds ip with wait=1, so the script blocks until the task has torn itself down. Used when a movie is aborted/ended explicitly, e.g. 'c4 c5 ca-loop c8-loop(until 0) c6' and right before scene transitions.

0xc7.name: movie_wait_end
0xc7.evidence: Module handler 0x800C0044: while the movie task exists it rewinds ip (waits a frame); if the task's 'finished' flag (bit 3) is set it also sets the close flag (bit 2). So it blocks until playback is finished and the task is gone. Typical sequence: c4, c5, loop on c8 until 2 (playing), c7, then sound stop (d7).

0xc8.name: movie_status
0xc8.evidence: Module handler 0x800C00B0: G[0] = -1 if no movie task, 0 if finished (flag bit 3), 2 if playing (flag bit 4), else 1 (loading/preparing). Scripts poll it: 'c8; push G0; ne 2; jump if !pop; 8c 1; jump back' (wait until playing), or loop while it is 1, or wait until 0.

0xc9.name: engine_set_param
0xc9.args: operand low16 = sub-op 0..11; 1 inline word (stack: sub-op on top, then value) = value. Sub-ops listed in notes.md (0 battle BGM id, 1 second BGM id, 2/8/10/11/6 flag bits in ctx+0x398, 3 scene tileset package, 4/5/7 unused, 9 battle start mode)
0xc9.evidence: Jump table 0x8007E0A4. Sub-op 3 (845 of 1,080 uses, 49 distinct ids 0x59E..0x5CE) is a package id: the preload task 0x80043C4C reads it, together with the fixed packages 1487 (0x5CF) and 1488/1489 (picked by a bit of the active character's item byte), into buffers kept at ctx+4/+0xC/+0x10. I decompressed 0x59E and 0x5C9: each is a 5-part package: a small table, an SLZ block that decompresses to MIPS code (jal targets 0x80081D8C, 0x80082368, 0x80060044, 0x80021C80, i.e. calls into the field engine), a ~200 KB 8bpp TIM (dark wood planks, bookshelves = interior tile textures) and a 4bpp TIM. So sub-op 3 selects the scene's tile graphics/map code module. Sub-op 0 holds a BGM directory word (script values 2249..2282 = the play_bgm id space; reset default 0x8C4): the loader preloads that file when it differs from ctx+0x38C (the id play_bgm last loaded); library func_09E7(battle, bgm, bgm2, flag) sets it (and sub 1) right before start_battle. Sub-op 9 ([0x8007FD89], values 1/3) is read inside start_battle (0x8004227C, 0x800423E8) and selects which of ctx+0x398 bits 4/8 are set (0 = decide from the situation, 2 -> 4, 3 -> 8). Sub-ops 2/8/10/11 (flag bits 2/0x100/0x1000/0x2000 of ctx+0x398) are written in clusters just before start_battle; no reader exists in the field engine, so the battle module reads them. Sub-op 6 (0x200, 156 uses, always 1) is set at scene start of dungeon scenes after 'play_bgm 0x8B3'. 4/5/7 have no uses.

0xca.name: movie_frame
0xca.evidence: Module handler 0x800C013C: if the movie task exists G[0] = the module's current-frame counter (word at 0x800C0C40), else G[0] = 0x7FFFFFFF. Scripts poll it to time effects: 'ca; push G0; lt N; wait' with thresholds 0x34,0x39,0x44,0x49 or 0x95,0x12B,0x172,0x219 followed by ba (screen effect), in the ending cut-scenes.

0xcb.name: caption
0xcb.evidence: record = low 16 bits; a one-line <5> place name in 87 of 88 uses

0xcc.name: treasure
0xcc.evidence: 6 inline words: position, item id, flags; the 5th is the "You found ..." record in 466 of 466 uses

0xcd.name: set_light
0xcd.args: 3 inline words: w0 (+ the instruction's low 16 bits) = three halfwords stored as the light vector (observed (0,0xF000,0) and (0,0x1000,0), i.e. straight down / up in 4.12 fixed); w1 and w2 low half = three halfwords of the light colour column; w2 high half = light index (0..2). Used in pairs (index 0 then 1) in the 3D scenes
0xcd.evidence: Handler 0x8006FE28 stores the values into arrays at 0x8007FCBC (vector) and 0x8007FCDC (3x3 halfword matrix, column = index) and calls 0x8007CDF4, which executes ctc2 into GTE control registers 16-20 = light colour matrix. 48 uses, always the same two calls (0xF000/0x1000 pair) at the start of a handful of scenes.

0xce.name: set_footstep_sfx
0xce.args: operand low16 = sfx id stored in ctx+0x390 (observed 0x48-0x4E; 0x4B in 670 of 871 uses); 1 inline word = sfx id stored in ctx+0x392 (0x51 or 0x52)
0xce.evidence: The only consumers of ctx+0x390/0x392 are 0x8006AEEC and the scene-reset code (defaults 0x48 and 0x51). 0x8006AEEC walks a pointer table at 0x80080608 (selected by [0x8007FD7E], e.g. entries at 0x800805D8) of 3-byte entries (animation id, frame A, frame B) and, when the actor's animation id and frame number match, plays that sfx id with the positional-sfx routine 0x80059180 at the actor's position (id 0x392 for animations 0x25/0x26, id 0x390 otherwise, or the floor type from the controlled actor). 871 uses, one per scene as scene set-up.

0xcf.name: stop_sfx
0xcf.args: 1 stack value: sound/voice id (as returned in G[0] by the play ops, e.g. 0x8F, and held in a local)
0xcf.evidence: Pops one value and calls 0x8001A174(sound engine [0x8007FD9C], id). Despite its label (note_on_activate_voice) that routine, when read, zeroes the sequence slot (stride 52 at +0x112C) and keys off every voice (24) belonging to it - the same call op 0xD7 makes with a stopped stream's id. Scripts do 'push L0xc; cf' shortly before a scene change (fade-out, wait, stop, load next scene), where the local came from an earlier play op.

0xd0.name: set_camera_limits
0xd0.args: operand low byte: 0 = also clamp the camera now, nonzero = only store; 2 inline words: (min_x | min_y<<16), (max_x | max_y<<16); negative values mean default (0 for the minima, map width/height [0x8007FC74/76] for the maxima)
0xd0.evidence: Handler 0x8006FF74 stores four halfwords at ctx+200..206 after replacing negatives, and when the operand is 0 clamps the current camera position (camera struct at [0x8007F100]+0x168+idx*60, +16/+20, = +24/+28 >> 8) to the stored limits. Typical call 'd0 1, 0x60ffff, 0xffffffff' = left/top limits only.

0xd1.name: actor_set_sort_params
0xd1.args: operand low16 = actor id (0xFFFF = current actor); 1 inline word: low byte -> actor+0x102, next byte -> actor+0x103 (observed 0x3800, 0x3802, 0x1902, 0x6403, ...)
0xd1.evidence: Handler 0x80070154 stores the two bytes. +0x102 is initialised from [0x8007FD46] at actor creation and its bit 0 selects the depth value in the actor draw routine 0x80038278: bit0 clear -> 0x80038154 result + 0x100, bit0 set -> the plain result (an ordering-table depth bias between the actor and the map layers); script values for +0x102 are 0, 2 or 3. +0x103 (the 0x19..0x64 byte, initialised from [0x8007FD44]) is written at 0x80036770 and 0x800701C4 and read nowhere in this overlay. Meaning of the second byte unknown; first byte = draw depth/priority bias is the best reading. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live, scene 0x1B, real handler run from a patched script): stores confirmed (0x2803 -> +0x102/+0x103 = 03/28, etc.). Defaults come from the map's control layers 3/4 at load (0x8006B870/0x8006B884: hall 0x28/0, scene 0x16 0x14/2). +0x102 bit 0: in 0x80038278 the occluder baseline depth at the actor's x gets +0x100 (one pixel row) when clear; compared with the actor's bbox bottom at 0x80038400-0x80038478, so it is a one-pixel front/behind tie-break against the wall layer. On the balcony both actors stand ~0.65 px behind the line, so ~100 screenshots over all values showed no change. +0x103: no reader anywhere in resident RAM, the field overlay or the 51 scene code packages; scene 0x38 steps it 0x20..0x50 on a walking actor, so a per-position depth/priority value whose consumer is elsewhere. Still low.

0xd2.name: update_sfx_position
0xd2.args: operand low byte = voice id (as returned by a positional sfx start); 2 inline words: x | y<<16, volume | param<<16 (or 5 stack values)
0xd2.evidence: Handler 0x800701C8 unpacks the arguments and calls 0x800593EC(voice, x, y, vol, param), the same routine the actor-attached sfx task (0x8003B734, op 0xDB) calls every frame to re-pan and re-attenuate a playing voice from a map position relative to the camera (centre 160,112). Only 12 uses.

0xd3.name: sound_seq_load
0xd3.args: operand low16 = resource id (0x937, 0xDC4 x27, 0xA98, 0xBBD, 0xDB3-0xDFD...); result = handle (0-127, round robin) in accumulator G[0], scripts store it in a local
0xd3.evidence: Handler 0x800702AC calls 0x8005A014(id), which allocates a task (function 0x8005A098) and returns its handle. The task state machine waits for the CD to be idle, asks cd_get_track_sector_info for the resource, mallocs a buffer (task+8) and starts the CD read (cd_set_play_location/cd_set_play_mode), then in state 2 polls the sound engine (0x8001A100) and clears task+15 when the sequence ends. Ops d4/d6/d7 take this handle; d4 hands the buffer to 0x80019834 (sequence_parse_events), so the loaded data is a music/sound sequence. Ids are adjacent to the movie ids used by c4 (the audio that goes with a movie).

0xd4.name: sound_seq_play
0xd4.args: 4 stack values (top first): handle (from d3), x (-1 = no positioning), y or pan, volume. Typical: push 0x7f, push 0 or 0x7f, push -1, push handle
0xd4.evidence: Handler 0x80070324 finds the d3 task via 0x800702D4; while its state is < 2 (still loading) it rewinds ip by 4 and restores the stack pointer (waits and retries). Then, if x != -1, derives pan/volume from the position with 0x80059084 (relative to the camera), else uses the given values; calls 0x8003E134 -> 0x80019834 (sequence_parse_events) on the loaded buffer and stores the returned sequence id in task+15. Pairs of calls with pan 0 and pan 0x7F on two handles are used as a stereo pair around movies.

0xd5.name: sound_seq_set_position
0xd5.args: 4 stack values popped (top first): handle (from d3), x, y, volume; NEVER used in scene code
0xd5.evidence: Handler 0x80070460 looks up the d3 task by handle (0x800702D4) and, if its sequence slot byte (+0xF) is not 0xFF, calls 0x800593EC(slot, x, y, volume, 0x2000) - the same routine op 0xD2 (update_sfx_position) uses for plain sfx voices, and the one the actor sfx task 0x8003B734 calls every frame to re-pan/re-attenuate from the map position relative to the camera. So it is the position update for a positional sound sequence started with d3/d4. Mechanism from code; never used.

0xd6.name: sound_is_playing
0xd6.args: 1 stack value: handle from d3; result in accumulator G[0] (0 = finished / unknown handle)
0xd6.evidence: Handler 0x8007050C finds the d3 task and stores 0x8001A100(sound engine, task+15) in G[0]; that routine returns the sequence slot's +0x1130 word (0 for an inactive slot). Scripts use it as a wait loop: 'push handle; d6; push G0; jump if !pop; 8c 1; jump back'.

0xd7.name: sound_seq_stop
0xd7.evidence: Handler 0x8007058C finds the d3 task, frees its data buffer (free(task+8)), stops the playing sequence with 0x8001A174(engine, task+15) when it is valid, and zeroes the task function pointer (kills the task). Appears after c7/c6 (movie end) with the two handles from d3, and before scene changes.

0xd8.name: set_battle_return_scene
0xd8.args: operand low16 = scene id; 2 inline words: x | y<<16 (stored raw), facing byte. The position and facing are overwritten by start_battle (0x800364F0 at 0x80042694) with the hero's, so they have no effect
0xd8.evidence: Handler 0x8006FB44 writes ctx+0x318 = scene id, ctx+0x312 = table[id].dir word, ctx+0x314 = 0x8006B228(...), ctx+0x94/+0x98 = x/y, ctx+0x39B = byte (live values at Valhalla: ctx+0x318 = 0x16 = the current scene, +0x312 = 0xE30 = 3632 = 3610+0x16, +0x314 = 0xE16) and sets [0x8007F260] |= 0x2000. That flag is tested in start_battle 0x8004227C (0x800426A8): with it set ctx+0x39A = 4, ctx+0x38C (current BGM id) = -1 and ctx+0x24 = 0, else ctx+0x39A = 2. The single use (scene 0xEB, the sluice-gate/final area) is 'd8 0xEC (0x01A8013B, 0); func_09E7(battle 0x43B, bgm 0x8D2, ...); wait 60; select_scene 0xEC; change_scene 0x01A8013B' i.e. it stages the destination scene and arrival position before a scripted boss battle. Hypothesis, one use only. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): it writes the same fields as the normal enter-scene function 0x8006C9DC (ctx+0x318 id, +0x312 dir word, +0x314 shared package, +0x94/+0x98, +0x39B) and sets F260 bit 0x2000, which start_battle (0x800426C0) turns into ctx+0x39A = 4 (fresh scene entry; 2 = resume after battle, 3 = menu, 5 = world map) with ctx+0x38C = -1, ctx+0x24 = 0; the flag is cleared at 0x800427C0 (one-shot). The battle module's exit (0x8005F560..0x8005F884 in a mid-battle RAM image) loads packages ctx+0x314 and ctx+0x312 and restarts the field engine (package 2292). Test: Valhalla intro script patched to 'd8 0xEC' + func_09E7 battle; after winning, scene 0xEC (golden sluice gate) loaded and its cutscene played; with id 0x16 Valhalla restarted fresh. So in scene 0xEB the lines after func_09E7 never run on a win. Defeat not tested (code: 0x8006C85C picks exit code 0/1/2 from ctx+0x398 bits).

0xd9.name: spawn_ambient_sound_source
0xd9.args: operand byte0 = first voice index, byte1 = last voice index (0xFF in byte0 = update an existing source: byte1 = the source id that d9 returned in G[0]); 2 inline words (or 5 stack values): word0 = x (low16, 0xFFFF = fixed) | y or fixed-pan/volume (high16), word1 = nonzero starts at full volume (zero fades in from 0); G[0] = source id (counter ctx+0xFF9, 0..127)

0xda.name: play_sfx_at_actor
0xda.args: operand low16 = actor id; word0 = sfx id (low16) | byte (bits 16-23, volume-like, e.g. 0x7F); word1 low half = extra param (signed byte passed to the sound call) (2 inline words or 3 stack values)
0xda.evidence: Shared handler 0x80076964 queues command type 15 on the actor. Executor 0x8003B584 calls 0x80059180(id, actor x, actor y, byte, param). 0xdb.name: attach_sfx_to_actor
0xdb.args: operand low16 = actor id; word0 = sfx id (low16) | volume byte (bits 16-23) | tag byte (bits 24-31); word1 low half = extra param (2 inline words or 4 stack values)
0xdb.evidence: Queues command type 16. Executor 0x8003B5D8 creates a task (function 0x8003B734) bound to the actor (+36) holding id (+44), tag (+46), volume (+48), param (+50). 0xdd.name: actor_set_prop_or
0xdd.args: stack form (107 uses, all of the same shape): pop actor id, pop property id (e.g. 0x26), then pop four words that are OR-ed together into the value; the inline form takes (property id, value) like op 0xA1

Executor 0x8003A5C8 dispatches on the id through two jump tables (0x8007D8A8 and 0x8007D988 / 0x8007DA78, ~60 property setters: position +0x94/+0x98, byte +0xC2/+0xC6, +0xD8, model lookup +0xCC, flags +0xE4 ...). 0xde.args: operand low16 = sfx id (11 of 13 uses are id 9; also 7, 0xB); no other arguments

0xdf.name: bgm_save_state
0xdf.evidence: Handler 0x800709DC copies ctx+0x18 into the sound engine structure ([0x8007FD9C]+0x1C) and sets its byte +5 = 1. The BGM preload task does the same thing inline when ctx+0x38E (c9 sub-op 1) == -1 (0x800435D0..0x800435F8), so the pair looks like 'point the sound engine at the preloaded music data'. ctx+0x18 is a heap pointer (zero in the Valhalla snapshot). Dead built-in; purpose still a guess. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): sets sound manager +0x1C = ctx+0x18 (a 2,144-byte buffer allocated at New Game, 0x8003C5B4; the pointer is non-zero, only its contents start zero) and +5 = 1. The sound tick 0x80015754 treats +5 as 'save' (0x80015A50: 24 channel records mgr+0x98..0x8D8, the music data pointer mgr+0x30, volumes/pans, 3 bytes, [mgr+0x30]+4) and +4 as 'restore' (0x80015B04). Live: after 'df' the buffer went from 0 to 756 non-zero bytes, 477 of 528 words equal to mgr+0x98.., buf+0x840 = mgr+0x30 = 0x801FB000. The preload task does the same save before battles (0x800435F8) and so does 0x8005F7E4. No code sets +4 (restore) in the EXE, field overlay or battle image: the snapshot appears never restored in this build (title/menu/world-map modules not searched).

0xe0.name: set_portrait_default_side
0xe0.args: value in instruction low 16 bits (inline, always 0/1 in scripts) or 1 popped; nonzero = set, 0 = clear
0xe0.evidence: Handler 0x80075C5C sets/clears bit 27 (0x08000000) of [0x8007F260]. 2,232 of its 4,499 uses are in library func_033C (message placement): anchor 0 and 3 -> 'e0 1', anchors 1 and 2 -> 'e0 0' right before 0x92/0x93/0x94 (anchors 8-15 pick 1/0 from the facing byte of that actor). The only reader in the field overlay is the text renderer 0x8004BF6C at 0x8004C860: when a line slot (box+0x4A6..) is armed with the mode value -1 it copies that bit into message-box flag bit 0 (box+0x338), otherwise it sets/clears bit 0 from the mode. Box flag bit 0 is tested at 0x8004E6F4 in the portrait drawing routine (the buffer at box+0x32C loaded by 0xA8): set = the portrait is built from textured quads (GPU 0x2C/0x2E, routine 0x8004E334, vertex x = width - tile x, i.e. mirrored), clear = plain sprite rectangles (0x64/0x66, routine 0x8004DFEC). LIVE (scene 0x1B patched into place, Frei's line 'Welcome to Valhalla', box flags +0x338 = 0x08220001 at 0x800FD0F0): (1) forcing the e0 argument 1 -> 0 at the call changed nothing (0 differing pixels 90 frames later); (2) clearing box bit 0 by hand changed nothing in 2 frames; (3) setting it again made Frei's portrait jump from the bottom-left to the bottom-right of the screen, mirrored. So bit 0 does control portrait mirroring/side, but e0's value at the start of the line did not change the picture, so when the renderer re-samples it (only when a slot is re-armed with mode -1) was not pinned down. Name changed from set_msgbox_flag: what it does to the portrait is medium confidence, the exact trigger is not understood. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (edited discs in TinyPSX, scene 0x1B record 14): the bit only matters for lines whose text command 19 has the value ffff; 0000/0100 set the side themselves, which is why (1) showed nothing on Frei's <19:0100> line. With the line changed to <19:ffff>: x anchor 0 (e0 1) -> portrait bottom left; anchor 2 (same x = 24, e0 0) -> bottom right, mirrored, with the box pixel-identical; <19:0100> with anchor 2 -> identical to anchor 0; anchor 1 (box on the right, e0 0) -> bottom right. 1 = left, 0 = right (mirrored): the default portrait side, which func_033C sets to the box's side.

0xe1.evidence: Handler 0x80070A1C stores the 4 bytes into ctx+0x39C..0x39F; for each slot whose id changed it sets the old actor's role byte (+217 of the 236-byte actor entry, table [0x8007F1E4], 25 entries) to 1 and the new actor's to 2, clears some motion/flag bits, calls the per-slot func_8001AAE8 and then pokes an object (func_8002FD10 + func_80059568). 0xe4.name: set_character_weapon
0xe4.args: 1-based roster index (ins low16 or popped); item id: 1 inline word or popped; -1 = query only; G[0] = previous id
0xe4.evidence: Handler 0x80070D2C: entry = [0x8007F1E4] + 236*(idx-1), i.e. the same 25-record roster table as b2/e1 (not the 264-byte actor table); G[0] = old halfword at entry+20, then (unless -1) stores the new value, looks it up in the 3-byte table [0x8007F204] (also used by e5/e6) and builds 3 'mode' slots at +157..159; for index 1 it also flips movement flag bits at +156. In the roster records the halfword at +20 is the first of a list of ids (e.g. 0x49 0xAA 0xB4 0xBE 0xC3), so it is more likely an equipped weapon/attack id than a generic item. 4 uses (scenes 0x6F, 0x3EC, 0x3EE): 'e4 5 0x61 ... push L0 ... e4' save/restore and 'e4 1 -1' compared with 0x100. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): +20 is equipment slot 0 of 10 (+20..+38; 0x8006660C scans them); slot 0 is the weapon: the 3-byte table [0x8007F204] per item id-1 has the item class in byte 0 (1 sword, 2 polearm/axe, 3 axe/rapier, 4 wand, 6 bow). Byte 1 bit 7 (ranged) sets +156 bit 2, else bit 0; bits 4-6 give up to 3 mode ids at +157..159 (current at +155). The battle preload 0x80043490 reads roster[0]+20 and loads package 1489 (bow) instead of 1488. Test: 'e4 1 0x106' (Elven Bow) then a battle started from a patched script: Lenneth holds a bow; with a sword or wand she holds a sword (scratchpad bi/actor/bw_cmp3.png). The field sprite does not change. Uses: Arngrim (5) given item 0x61 for a guest battle then restored (scene 0x6F); scene 0x3EC checks whether Lenneth holds 0x100, the Demon Sword Levantine; scene 0x3EE gives her sword 0x16A.

0xe5.name: has_item
0xe5.args: item id: inline = ins low 16 bits (0 inline words) or 1 popped; result in G[0] (1 = held, 0 = not)
0xe5.evidence: Handler 0x80070F10 scans the 612-slot inventory in the big state struct (halfword ids at ctx+0x3C6, byte counts at ctx+0x88E) for the id and returns 1 if the matching slot's count is nonzero, else 0. Used as 'e5 0x4f; jump if !G0 ...; e6 0x4f -1; loop' (drain all copies) and as a gate ('e5 0x263', 'e5 0x25a').

0xe6.name: add_item
0xe6.args: item id: inline = ins low 16 bits, stack = top of stack; delta (signed count): 1 inline word / 2nd stack pop (negative removes)
0xe6.evidence: Handler 0x80070FAC calls func_8005EC08(id, delta, maxbyte = item_table[id*3-1], 1): finds the id in the 612-slot inventory (ctx+0x3C6 / ctx+0x88E), inserts it in the first free slot if absent and delta>0, adds delta, and deletes the slot (compacting the 16-entry equipped list at ctx+0x328) when the count reaches <=0. 1116 of 1129 uses are the shared library's item-grant helper ('push 1; push L0; e6' right after a message + sys_7e); scenes use 'e6 0x263 -1', 'e6 0x25a -1' (consume key items before 'You found the Accursed Flame Gem') and 'e6 1 10' (give 10 of item 1).

0xe7.name: play_sfx_pos_tracked
0xe7.args: inline: 2 words (ins low 16 = sfx id; word1 = x(low16), y(high16); word2 = volume(low16), extra byte (bits 16-23)); stack form pops 5: id, x, y, volume, extra. Returns the voice handle byte in G[0] (0xFF = none)
0xe7.evidence: Handler 0x80078C6C calls func_800591F8, which (unless sound is gated by flags 0x8007F25C&0x84000 / 0x8007F260&0x200) finds a free entry in the 8-byte handle table at 0x80080140, calls func_80059180 (the same positional-sfx routine op 0x8F calls: func_80059084 derives pan/volume from x,y relative to the camera centre 160,112, then func_8003E0D0 -> sound player 0x80019B70) and stores the handle. Scripts pair it with 8F (same args, e.g. 'sys_8f 0x7e ... 7f' / 'sys_e7 0x7d ... 7f'), keep G0 in a variable (G0x1F1.b) and later pass it to e9.

0xe8.name: add_evaluation_level
0xe8.args: signed 16-bit delta: ins low 16 bits, or popped; no clamp
0xe8.evidence: Handler 0x80071044: ctx.halfword[0x388] += arg (no clamp). The only other code touching it is the HUD routine at 0x800601C8..0x80060244: +1 per frame (cap 100) while idle, -5 per frame (floor 0) while the other state is active, with a bar drawn at (58,32) by 0x80060948 in the same routine; the same routine adds G0x68.b*500+100 to G[0x20] (capped at 999,999,999) when it fires. A 0..100 recharge-style gauge; what it is called in game is unknown. Purely mechanical name. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): ctx.h[0x388] is the Evaluation Level, the 'Eval.' line of the camp menu (reader lh 0x388 at 0x8005A620 in the menu module); New Game sets 100 (0x8003C6A0). Test: real built-in 'push 50; e8' then 'e8 0xFFFB': Eval 100 -> 145 in the menu. The routine at 0x800601C8 is not a HUD gauge: it is the Artifact prompt in per-actor task 0x8005EDFC (messages 3-6 of the shared records: 'This item is an Artifact...', 'Will you offer up the artifact to Lord Odin?'); Yes = Eval +1 (cap 100), No = -5 (floor 0); both add chapter*500+100 Event EXP to G[0x20] and show it via <14:00>. 0xe9.evidence: Handler 0x80078D5C -> func_80059370: if the handle is not 0xFF, looks it up in the 8-entry handle table at 0x80080140, calls func_8001A174(sound state, handle) (voice release / key-off path: reaches spu_keyon_keyoff and push_voice_event_queue) and marks the entry 0xFF. 0xea.name: restore_party_after_battle
0xea.evidence: Handler 0x8007109C loops over the 25 roster records [0x8007F1E4] (236 bytes each) and for those with role byte (+217) 1 or 2 clears halfword +214 and copies word +176 to +172 (the reset e3 does when its flag is nonzero). 3 uses (scenes 0x6E, 0x6F, 0x3EC), all at the end of a scripted walk: '... call func_09E7?; ea; c9 8 0; b2 0x103; e1 0 0; e3'. What +172/+176/+214 are (position / target / velocity of the follower) is not established. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): for roster records with role 1 or 2 it sets +172 = +176 and clears +214; roles 0 untouched (confirmed with poked values). New Game sets +172 = +176 = the max-HP-like values (1000, 6079, 2000...), and 0xE1 does 'if (+214 & 0x0D) { clear; if (+172 == 0) +172 = 1 }' on joining, a revive pattern, so +172 = current HP, +176 = max HP, +214 = status ailments is the reading. All 3 uses come right after func_09E7 (start_battle). HP was not seen on screen, so the HP/status meaning is medium-low; the mechanism is certain. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (menu test): roster record 0 (Lenneth, 0x801DFE9C) +172 set to 123 at the 0x8D hit -> camp menu shows 'DME 123 / 1000' with 123 in red; the same with the real built-in (ea000000 patched in before the scene change) -> 'DME 1000 / 1000'. +214 set to 0x00FF -> status-ailment icons (skull, purple bubbles, blue sparks, grey stone) on her party panel; with 0xEA the field reads 0 and her normal sprite shows. So +172 = current HP (DME), +176 = max HP, +214 = status ailment bits; single bits 1/2/4/8 showed nothing on the first menu page, which has no sprite until the cursor moves. Scripts: scratchpad bi/eahp.

0xeb.name: add_materialize_points
0xeb.args: signed 32-bit amount: 1 inline word, or popped when bit 20 is set; no clamp
0xeb.evidence: Handler 0x800710E8: ctx.word[0xA4] += arg. LIVE: a watch on 0x801F5F80 shows the field is first written at frame 2055 by the New Game initialisation code (0x8003C77C in the title/new-game module): ctx+0xA4 = 2000 and ctx+0xA8 = 0, in the same routine that clears the 1,176-byte map-exploration bitmap at ctx+0xAF2, sets the party slots ctx+0x39C, and initialises the 25 roster records - so ctx is the persistent game-state block, not just a script context. UPDATE 2026-11-12 (live): ctx+0xA4 is Materialize Points, the 'Materialize point' figure in the camp menu (reader lw 0xA4 at 0x8005A4E8 in menu draw 0x80059EE0). Poking 12345 showed 'Materialize point 12345'; the real built-in ('push 1000; eb' then 'eb 0 0xEA') gave 3234 = 2000 + 1000 + 234. So func_030A's chapter*300 on a party join and scene 0x447's +20000 are MP rewards.

0xec.name: set_map_exploration_tracking
0xec.args: value = instruction low byte (always 0 in the 22 uses): 0 = tracking OFF (sets bit 9 of [0x8007F264]), nonzero = on; 0 inline words
